name: Toast
summary: A short message that slides in at the bottom end corner, stacks with others and leaves on its own, built by Vectra.toast().
description: Use a toast to confirm something that just happened (saved, copied, archived), with an optional action such as Undo. Do not put anything people must act on in a toast; use an alert or a dialog for that.

classes.name: v-toast-region
classes.description: The stack, pinned to the bottom end corner in the top layer. Made by the JS.

classes.name: v-toast
classes.description: One toast: a tone dot, the text, an optional action and a close button.

classes.name: v-toast-action
classes.description: An optional text button, such as Undo or Retry.

classes.name: v-toast-close
classes.description: The close button; the cross is drawn in CSS. Needs aria-label.

classes.name: v-toast-danger
classes.description: Danger dot; the message is announced assertively.

states.description: Set while a toast fades out, just before it is removed.
Set on toasts past the first three; they wait their turn.

api.signature: Vectra.toast(message, { tone, action: { label, onClick }, undo, duration }) => { dismiss }
api.description: Shows a toast. tone is 'success', 'info', 'warning' or 'danger'. undo is a shortcut for an Undo action. duration is in ms (default 5000, at least 10000 with an action, 0 to stay until closed). Returns dismiss() to close it early.

keyboard.action: Moves into the toast to its action and close buttons. Timers pause while focus is inside.
Runs the action or closes the toast.

a11y: Every message is read out through a polite live region, or an assertive one for tone danger; the action label is added, for example "Project archived. Undo available."
A toast with an action stays at least 10 seconds, and all timers pause while the stack is hovered or focused (WCAG 2.2.1).
The tone dot is decoration; the words carry the meaning.
When a focused toast closes, focus moves to the next toast instead of being lost.

examples.title: Live toasts
examples.description: Each button calls Vectra.toast(). Open more than three to see the queue.
examples.html:
<button class="v-btn v-btn-primary" type="button" id="toast-saved">Saved</button>
<button class="v-btn v-btn-secondary" type="button" id="toast-undo">Archive with undo</button>
<button class="v-btn v-btn-danger" type="button" id="toast-retry">Error with retry</button>
<button class="v-btn v-btn-secondary" type="button" id="toast-many">Five at once</button>
